analyzed_vuln.description: `php_hash_unserialize` accepts attacker-controlled serialized `HashContext` state and restores algorithm internals (including xxh64 `memsize`) without enforcing invariant bounds. Later, `hash_update()` calls `PHP_XXH64Update` -> `XXH64_update`, which uses `state->memsize` in `32 - state->memsize` and memcpy length calculations. With forged `memsize` > 32, this underflows to a huge size_t and triggers an out-of-bounds read in `XXH_memcpy`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Input to `php-fuzz-unserializehash` must unserialize into a `HashContext` object for algorithm `xxh64` with crafted internal state array values (notably an oversized memsize field). The harness then calls `hash_update($ctx, <prefix data>)`; because context validation is missing during unserialization, the malformed state reaches `XXH64_update`, causing large memcpy/read and ASan heap-buffer-overflow.
